intent.objective: Design a governed research route that classifies implementation/domainspec content against the open-core commercial boundary defined in COMMERCIALIZATION-SYNTHESIS.md: the FREE WEDGE (validators/audits, spec->test derivation, taxonomy/relationships, code-tag extraction, Arcanum sigils, Necronomicon, Craft ledger schema, intent tools) is lifted into public arcanum; the PAID MOAT (CyberAlchemy governance engine, Craft deferred automation/metering, enforcement runtime, vendor-neutral attestation product, Golden Quill/Tilth vertical, the Lean formal-proof half) and the runtime layer stay private in domainspec. Produce a candidate integration research artifact and an explicit wedge-vs-moat boundary decision, not an executed migration.
intent.operator_sentence: Research, do not execute: split domainspec by the open-core boundary — free wedge becomes public arcanum, paid moat and runtime stay private — grounded in COMMERCIALIZATION-SYNTHESIS.md, and record the wedge-vs-moat decision before anything moves.

steps.name: Survey what arcanum already knows and what domainspec is
stop_conditions: Stop if an area is paid moat or runtime per COMMERCIALIZATION-SYNTHESIS.md; it stays private in domainspec.
Stop if arcanum already contains an equivalent capability.

steps.name: X-ray domainspec structure to expose contribution candidates
stop_conditions: Stop mapping at the subsystem boundary; tag each element by layer (runtime vs governance/agent/skills/concepts).

steps.name: Distill smallest governance/concept abstraction units
stop_conditions: Stop when each candidate unit names a recomposition target inside arcanum and stays decoupled from domainspec runtime.

steps.name: Resolve the open-core wedge-vs-moat boundary decision
stop_conditions: Stop and escalate to the user if any candidate is paid moat (CyberAlchemy engine, Craft automation/metering, enforcement runtime, attestation product, Golden Quill/Tilth, Lean formal-proof half) or cannot be decoupled from it.

steps.name: Extract source-first knowledge from the lean-formalization corpus

capability_metadata.role: source-first research tower over a corpus

inputs.ref: domainspec-lean-formalization/ (Lean formalization, theorems, taxonomy, novel-mappings, essays; separate git repo)

stop_conditions: Stop at source-backed claims and notation bridge; do not import the Lean proof runtime or scratch into arcanum.
Stop if the corpus yields no governance/concept-level knowledge distinct from domainspec.

steps.name: Distill the lean-formalization knowledge into reusable concept units
stop_conditions: Stop when each distilled unit names a recomposition target and stays decoupled from the Lean proof runtime.
Flag any unit that is part of the Lean formal-proof attestation moat (per COMMERCIALIZATION-SYNTHESIS.md §3/§9) for the wedge-vs-moat decision; do not auto-route it to public arcanum.

steps.name: Author the candidate research artifact
stop_conditions: Stop at a research artifact with candidate findings and residue; do not perform the migration.
Stop if the wedge-vs-moat decision did not approve any lift into arcanum.

gates.condition: arcanum and implementation/domainspec are separate submodules; the runtime layer stays in domainspec, only free-wedge governance/agent-work/skills/concepts are candidates for arcanum, and submodule-first commit discipline applies.

Paid-moat assets per COMMERCIALIZATION-SYNTHESIS.md (CyberAlchemy governance engine, Craft deferred automation/metering, enforcement runtime, vendor-neutral attestation product, Golden Quill/Tilth vertical, the Lean formal-proof half) must NOT be lifted into public arcanum; only the free wedge crosses.
This route produces candidate research only and does not claim promotion authority for inventory, ontology, glossary, sigil, or spell artifacts.
Any lift of governance/agent-work/skills/concepts from domainspec into arcanum requires explicit user approval before content is moved.
The s04 open-core wedge-vs-moat boundary decision must be resolved before the research artifact is authored.

subagent_strategy.trigger: domainspec spans many independent subsystems (framework, docs, experiments, governance, tools); mapping and distilling public-safe candidates per subsystem fits a fan-out shape.
subagent_strategy.explanation: Parallel subsystem mappers can each x-ray one domainspec area and propose candidate abstractions, while a boundary classifier flags private-only content, so the parent can synthesize a single candidate set without one agent holding the whole tree.
context: domainspec is a large private submodule with many top-level areas.
The open/private boundary is the dominant risk, so a dedicated classifier role is warranted.
Research only: no agent may move or commit content across the boundary.

roles.purpose: X-ray one domainspec subsystem and propose public-safe abstraction candidates.
roles.owns: Per-subsystem structure map and candidate list

roles.purpose: Classify each mapped element against the open-core boundary: free wedge (candidate for public arcanum) vs paid moat or runtime (stays private in domainspec), grounded in COMMERCIALIZATION-SYNTHESIS.md.
Build a source-first tower over the lean-formalization corpus and distill its concept-level knowledge, leaving the Lean proof runtime behind.

subagent_strategy.permission_prompt: Spawn parallel subsystem-mapper and boundary-classifier subagents to x-ray domainspec and propose public-safe abstraction candidates? They will only read and propose; no content crosses the boundary without your approval.

agents.receipt_artifact: arcanum/research/domainspec-integration/README.md (Part B) — Lean distilled units under moat protection

boundaries.contract: Only free-wedge governance, agent-work, skills, and concept abstractions (per COMMERCIALIZATION-SYNTHESIS.md) may be referenced toward arcanum; the paid moat and runtime layer stay private in domainspec and are referenced by handle, never copied.

Only generic engineering concepts from the lean-formalization corpus that are NOT part of the paid attestation moat may be referenced toward arcanum; the Lean formal-proof/attestation half (per COMMERCIALIZATION-SYNTHESIS.md §3/§9), proof runtime, scratch, and experiments stay private and are referenced by handle, never copied.
Lifting any layer into arcanum requires explicit user approval recorded as a decision before authoring.

promotion_splits.rule: Only free-wedge governance/agent-work/skills/concept abstractions (per COMMERCIALIZATION-SYNTHESIS.md) may cross, and only after explicit user approval; the paid moat and runtime stay private, no automatic crossing, and no claim of canonical knowledge promotion.

promotion_guardrails: Research findings remain candidate-level; they do not become canonical inventory, ontology, glossary, sigil, or spell knowledge without owner review.

Open-core boundary (COMMERCIALIZATION-SYNTHESIS.md): give away the wedge, sell the trust. Only the free wedge crosses to public arcanum; the paid moat (CyberAlchemy engine, Craft automation/metering, enforcement runtime, attestation product, Golden Quill/Tilth, Lean formal-proof half) and the runtime stay private in domainspec, with explicit user approval under submodule-first discipline.
